intent: Remove pr-ci-health's `push: branches: [main]` trigger. It rebased every conflict-free behind-main PR on every merge to main, and each rebase relaunches that PR's full workflow set. Its stated premise -- 'require branches up to date' making a behind-main PR unmergeable -- no longer holds, so the cost bought nothing.

commit.message: fix(ci): stop pr-ci-health rebasing the backlog on every merge to main

interface_mismatches: The trigger encoded a branch-protection assumption ('require branches up to date') in a workflow that never verifies it. When the setting changed, the workflow kept paying its cost with no way to notice.
honest_blockers: THIS REDUCES THE WAVES, IT DOES NOT END THEM. The hourly cron still runs `all`, which still includes the rebase step. Rebases go from once-per-merge to once-per-hour. Ending them entirely means gating the rebase step too, which is a larger change and removes a capability.

The premise claim rests on ONE observation: PR #1227 was behind main and reported mergeable_state 'unstable', not 'behind'. I could not read the branch-protection settings directly. If 'require branches up to date' is in fact still enabled, removing this trigger means behind-main PRs wait up to 59 minutes for the cron instead of ~1 minute. Annoying, not dangerous, and revertible.
CEREMONY ORDER WAS VIOLATED AND THIS RECEIPT SAYS SO: the edit and its test were authored before this packet existed. Read the binding as scope CONFORMANCE.
Not verified against a real merge-to-main. The proof is the next merge producing no wave, which I cannot schedule.
